protein: ParLQ, a protoglobin engineered for non-native carbene transfer; it is ParPgb carrying W59L and Y60Q, and the construct includes a C-terminal LE-His6 tag
readout: Fraction of cyclopropane product formed as the cis-2a diastereomer, cis/(cis+trans)
assay_method: Whole-cell cyclopropanation of styrene with ethyl diazoacetate in 96-well plate format, product quantified by chromatography against an internal standard; five active-site residues (56, 57, 59, 60, 89) were randomized and variants identified by evSeq. Parent and 395 variants across an initial site-saturation set and two rounds of active-learning-selected combinations.
remark: The reference sequence is ParLQ translated from the supplementary DNA of Table S1, 199 residues including the C-terminal LE-His6 tag, and positions 56, 57, 59, 60 and 89 read WYLQF, matching the parent code the source data uses; no UniProt entry for ParPgb was found, so the sequence rests on the supplement alone. Variants are named in the source by a five-letter code over the randomized sites and are converted to substitution labels against the parent, a code letter equal to the parent residue contributing nothing; the parent's own code WYLQF becomes the WT row. The readout is derived as the cis-2a yield divided by the sum of the cis and trans yields, which isolates selectivity from how much product formed at all; the lowest total yield in the set is 3.6 percent, so the ratio is defined throughout, and one variant with a slightly negative cis yield gives a slightly negative fraction that is kept as measured. Not extracted from this paper: the trans-2a yield on its own, which the source provides but which has no higher-is-better orientation, since the paper treats more trans product as worse rather than better; the plate-normalized ALDE objective, which is a restatement of the same pair of yields; and the public benchmark landscapes the paper runs simulations on, which belong to the publications that measured them.
